'''Melaku Worede''' ({{Langx|am|መላኩ ወረደ}}; 1936 – 31 July 2023) was an Ethiopian geneticist and agronomist.

Melaku was born in 1936,<ref name=livelihood/> in [[Shewa]], [[Ethiopia]], to [[Qeñazmach]] Worede Gebrekidan, an Ethiopian Shewan governor, army commander and aristocrat from Bulga, and [[Woizero]] Amsale Wodajeneh, an Ethiopian noblewoman from Shewa and the daughter of [[Fitawrari]] Wodajeneh Awgechaw, who was an army commander and viceroy of [[Ras Lul Seged]] in Ethiopia's former [[Solomonic dynasty]] Kingdom.

== Education and career ==
Melaku travelled to the US in the 1960s to pursue post-graduate studies. He obtained a PhD in [[Agronomy]] with a focus on plant genetics and breeding from the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Feyissa |first=Regassa |last2=Hodgkin |first2=Toby |date=2023-08-31 |title=Melaku Worede, crop genetics leader (1936–2023) |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-023-02735-x |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=621 |issue=7977 |pages=33–33 |doi=10.1038/d41586-023-02735-x|url-access=subscription }}</ref> 

Melaku was awarded the [[Right Livelihood Award]] in 1989 "for preserving Ethiopia's genetic wealth by building one of the finest seed conservation centres in the world."<ref name=livelihood>{{cite web |title=Melaku Worede (Ethiopia) |url=http://www.rightlivelihood.org/worede.html |publisher=Right Livelihood Award |accessdate=19 February 2011 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101130143727/http://rightlivelihood.org/worede.html |archivedate=30 November 2010 }}</ref>

Melaku features in the film ''Seeds of Justice''<ref>[http://www.seedsoffreedom.info Seeds of Freedom]</ref> which was released in June 2012, and features narration from Oscar-winning actor [[Jeremy Irons]]. The film was produced by The Gaia Foundation and the African Biodiversity Network, both organisations with whom Melaku has been a long-term ally and worked alongside to lead a number of trainings with Field Officers working across Africa. Melaku has three children: Mary Worede, H/Mariam Melaku Worede and Lij Tedla Melaku Worede.

==Death==
On 31 July 2023, the Ethiopian Biodiversity Institute (EBI) announced that Melaku had died.<ref>{{cite web |title=Laureate Dr. Melaku Worede, Pioneer of Biodiversity Conservation, Passes Away |url= https://addisinsight.net/laureate-dr-melaku-worede-pioneer-of-biodiversity-conservation-passes-away/ |website= addisinsight.net |date=31 July 2023 |access-date=1 August 2023}}</ref><ref name=addisstandard>{{cite web |title=Tribute: Remembering Dr. Melaku Worede: A pioneer crop diversity conservationist and farmers' rights advocate |first1=Teshome |last1=Hunduma   |first2=Bayush |last2=Tsegaye |url=https://addisstandard.com/tribute-remembering-dr-melaku-worede-a-pioneer-in-crop-diversity-conservationist-and-farmers-rights-advocate/ |website=addisstandard.com |date=1 August 2023 |access-date=1 August 2023}}</ref>
